title: Your Provident Fund Just Got a Boost: New Wage Ceiling Explained
description: India's EPFO has increased the mandatory wage ceiling for provident fund contributions. It has gone up from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 per month.

faq.q: What is the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF)?
faq.a: It's a mandatory retirement savings scheme for salaried employees in India, where both the employee and employer contribute a portion of the salary, which earns interest and can be withdrawn under specific conditions.

faq.q: Does this mean my pension will also increase?
faq.a: For those newly brought under mandatory EPS coverage (part of EPFO), yes, you will now start building eligibility for a pension. For existing members, your pension calculation is primarily based on your average monthly pay (capped at ₹15,000 for EPS contributions) and years of service, so the direct impact on the final pension payout needs to be assessed based on specific rules.

faq.q: What if my salary is above ₹25,000?
faq.a: If your basic wages are above ₹25,000, your mandatory EPF contribution will now be calculated on ₹25,000 (unless you and your employer mutually agree to contribute on your full salary, which is known as contributing above the statutory limit).

faq.q: When will I see this change in my salary slip?
faq.a: While the change is effective from September 17, 2026, employers may need one to two payroll cycles to update their systems. So, you might see the revised deductions reflect in your October or November 2026 salary slip, with potential arrears for the period from September 17.

faq.q: What should I do if I am affected by this change?
faq.a: Review your salary slip to understand the new deductions. While it reduces your immediate take-home pay, remember it's building a stronger financial cushion for your future.
